newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Central Bank posts $172 mln H1 net loss.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Central Bank posts $172 mln H1 net loss.

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank reported a net loss for the first half of 1997 of 85.3 billion bolivars ($172 million), over twice the 37 billion bolivar ($75 million) loss reported for the second half of 1996.

The loss was "directly due to the low return obtained on the Bank's most important assets, which did not cover the costs of monetary policy," the Bank said in a full page notice taken out in the national press.

Debt totaling 1.3 trillion bolivars owed by the National Deposits Debt Rescue Fund and a 1.4 trillion bolivar debt owed by the government currently pay the Central Bank low rates of interest, although they are among the Bank's largest assets.
However, the government is expected to shortly start issuing Treasury bills to pay its debt. The T-bills will be used to conduct open market operations.
The Bank currently issues its own paper, called Monetary Stabilization Notes, or TEMs, to conduct open market operations, and must pay interest on the bonds from its own account.
Some 2.5 trillion bolivars of TEMs are currently in circulation, the bank said.
